sentences.text: Gigantspinosaurus was a stegosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic Oxfordian stage in China, described by researchers as a medium-sized member of this group.
Estimates place this animal between 4.2 and 7 meters in length and weighing around 700 kilograms, though Gregory S. Paul estimated it was approximately 4.2 meters long and weighed 700 kilograms.
The neck plates of Gigantspinosaurus were small and triangular in shape.
Gigantspinosaurus had very broad hips and a fused plate formed by the neural spines of the sacral vertebrae and the first tail vertebra.
This dinosaur possessed robust forelimbs.
Each lower jaw held thirty teeth, suggesting a specific feeding strategy.
The first Gigantspinosaurus fossil was discovered in 1985 by Ouyang Hui and initially misidentified as Tuojiangosaurus in 1986.
Gigantspinosaurus sichuanensis was formally named by Ouyang in 1992 based on a lecture abstract.
The genus name Gigantspinosaurus combines Latin words for 'enormous' and 'spine' to describe its gigantic shoulder spines.
Gigantspinosaurus was widely considered a nomen nudum until 2006, when it was confirmed that the original abstract contained a valid description.
Public awareness of Gigantspinosaurus grew in 2006 after Tracy Ford published a reconstruction article treating it as a valid taxon.
The holotype specimen ZDM 0019 was found in the Upper Shaximiao Formation of Zigong, Sichuan, dating to the Oxfordian stage.
There is currently only one recorded fossil occurrence of Gigantspinosaurus.
Ford suggested that previous reconstructions showing shoulder spines pointing down were incorrect, proposing they extended upwards above the animal's back.
The presence of thirty teeth in each lower jaw indicates how the animal processed vegetation.
A 2018 redescription classified Gigantspinosaurus as an intermediate basal stegosaur sharing traits with both huayangosaurids and other stegosaurs.
Analysis found that Gigantspinosaurus was not the most basal stegosaur, as huayangosaurids like Chungkingosaurus and Huayangosaurus were considered more basal.
Gigantspinosaurus belongs to the family Huayangosauridae.
Gigantspinosaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
Gigantspinosaurus was a stegosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic Oxfordian stage in China, approximately 156 million years ago.
